api_adaptations: C pointer-plus-length inputs are immutable Rust byte slices; token offsets use XmlSpan { offset, length } and are lifetime-independent indices.
C output arrays become owned Vec<XmlToken> with capacity-limited entry points; an error returns an empty token vector and zero counts.
C out-pointers/status pairs become Result constructors, StreamStatus, and XmlResult values. take transfers the Vec once; Drop releases remaining storage.
C callbacks borrow each token only for the callback. Cancellation is sticky for XmlTokenStream and is polled at step entry, each validation byte, lexical parser loops, and visitor callbacks.

Streaming validates UTF-8 in bounded steps before grammar parsing to preserve C error precedence. Each parser step resumes stored lexical/tag/doctype state and advances at most the remaining byte budget; cancellation is polled within long text, attribute, comment, CDATA, PI, and doctype scans. It never calls tokenize_impl on the whole document.

Visitor mode uses fixed per-tag scratch for one start element and its bounded attributes, delivers those tokens when the tag closes, and retains no token vector across the document. visitor_storage_bytes reports allocated scratch capacity.
Rust slices make invalid non-null pointer/length pairs unrepresentable. InvalidArgument is retained in XmlError for API parity, but slice-based entry points cannot produce the C null-pointer case.

UTF-8 validation saves leading-byte offset, remaining continuation count and accumulated scalar across steps. Each input byte consumes budget and has a cancellation poll. Name parsing saves the incremental Utf8Scan decoder, leading-byte offset and QName classification, including the local first-scalar classification. Each scalar byte is read and pushed once during lexical decoding; equality rereads are separately charged and instrumented. Partial decoding and final QName classification do not reread a complete scalar.

Both one-shot cancelable entry points drive the real resumable stream parser with the caller limits and token capacity. Cancellation remains active during source validation and lexical parsing; there is no separate precancellation chunk pass followed by an uncancelable tokenizer.

Every terminal failed or canceled step clears retained tokens and tag scratch and zeros result counts. tokens returns an empty slice and take returns None. Failed and canceled statuses are sticky; visitor callbacks delivered before completion remain provisional until Complete.

PI exact-xml/ASCII-folded-xml classification and predefined entity classification are cached from accepted decoded scalars. Neither classification uses source-backed slices or eq_ignore_ascii_case after scanning.

End-name and duplicate-attribute equality use one fixed NameCompare state (two original-source spans, index, optional left byte). Both operands consume individual source-read budget units, with cancellation checks; no name copies are allocated. Equality steps may perform real work with no cursor advancement.

NameWork enforces a production budget on every variable token-name source load. Test total_reads includes lexical scanner reads plus comparison_reads; the existing reads counter remains the scanner component so prior assertions are preserved. All loads increment the appropriate component and the total at the actual source access, and decoder_inputs increments at byte pushes. Bounds are measured from actual totals rather than cursor progress; no slice/memcpy/eq source-name comparison bypasses this path in stream.rs.
intentionally_outside_scope: Namespace resolution, entity expansion, external resource access, and complete SVG decode/index behavior remain excluded by the frozen order.
The existing reader's complete-tag lexical contract does not certify full XML document validity.
remaining_review_gaps: The original C deterministic malformed-input fuzz loop is not ported; focused deterministic malformed cases remain covered.
Span tests cover representative emitted token kinds and byte boundaries, not every emitted span combination.
dependencies: std only; existing vexel-base dependency unchanged; no unsafe code, C shim, or unsupported-OS implementation
